rules.title: 2026 Annual General Adjustment rent increase limit
rules.requirement: Eligible landlords may raise the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% starting on January 1, 2026, but cannot increase rents for tenants whose tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025 and are covered by Costa‑Hawkins.
rules.coverage_conditions: eligible landlords; tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025; rents set pursuant to Costa‑Hawkins Rental Housing Act
rules.exemptions: tenants whose tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025 and whose rents are governed by Costa‑Hawkins
rules.quoted_span: allow eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026

rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services to set rental prices.
rules.quoted_span: Jersey City Code § 218-12 (effective June 2025) Prohibits a landlord’s use of algorithmic rent coordination services; includes public and private enforcement; fines up to $2,000 per day.

rules.title: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.requirement: Prohibits algorithmic rent setting
rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting

rules.title: Maximum tenant screening fee for 2026
rules.requirement: Landlords may not charge a tenant screening fee greater than $68.96 in the year 2026.
rules.coverage_conditions: for the calendar year 2026
rules.quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is $68.96

rules.title: Hoboken ban on algorithmic rent pricing software
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using software, algorithms, or data‑sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.
rules.quoted_span: Hoboken City Code, ch. 158-2 (effective July 2025) Prohibits landlords from using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.

rules.title: Screening fee cannot be charged when no unit is available
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge a prospective tenant a screening fee unless a rental unit is actually available, and must refund or not charge applicants not selected or not considered.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.

rules.title: Prevent algorithmic rent fixing in MA rental market
rules.requirement: Prohibits the use of algorithms to set or fix rental prices in the Massachusetts rental housing market.
rules.quoted_span: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market

rules.title: Prohibition of non‑refundable fees for existing tenants
rules.requirement: Owners or their agents may not charge a non‑refundable fee to an existing tenant for renewing a tenancy or for roommate changes.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy

rules.title: Ballot measure limiting annual rent increases
rules.requirement: Limits annual rent increases
rules.exemptions: exemptions for units operated solely for religious purposes
rules.quoted_span: limits annual rent increases for residences

rules.title: Mandatory tenant screening fee rights disclosure
rules.requirement: Before receiving a screening fee, the owner must provide a clear and conspicuous rights statement and the maximum fee cap.
rules.quoted_span: the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap

rules.title: Maximum security deposit amount for most landlords
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge only one month’s rent as a security deposit for both unfurnished and furnished units.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to most landlords as of July 1, 2024
rules.exemptions: none explicit
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

rules.title: Prohibition on Criminal History Inquiries and Discriminatory Actions
rules.requirement: Landlords in Berkeley may not inquire about, use, or base any rental decision on a applicant's or tenant's criminal history, including in advertisements, applications, or lease terms.
rules.coverage_conditions: rental housing providers in Berkeley
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; Public housing/Section 8 properties limited exemptions; Owner-occupied properties (1-3 units) where owner resides; Units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; Units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful to do any of the following with regard to current or prospective tenants Inquire about criminal history Indicate that persons with criminal backgrounds will not be considered for housing

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Coverage for Covered Units
rules.requirement: Landlords must have a legally valid reason (just cause) to evict tenants in covered units.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980; Single‑family homes with tenancies that began before 1996; Rooming houses (single‑family homes with five or more rooms rented out individually with separate leases); New construction units built after June 1980 that are partially covered; Single‑family homes with tenancies beginning on or after Jan 1 1996 that are partially covered; Most condominiums that are partially covered; Units with certain government subsidies that are partially covered
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplex (owner‑occupied duplex as of Dec 31 1979); Unit where owner shares a kitchen or bath with tenant if owner lived on the property at tenancy start; Tenancies started after Nov 7 2018 on properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner‑occupied; University rental units such as dormitories; Nonprofit cooperative
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

rules.title: Security Deposit Interest Requirement for Covered Units
rules.requirement: Security deposits for covered units must accrue interest.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980; Single‑family homes with tenancies that began before 1996; Rooming houses (single‑family homes with five or more rooms rented out individually with separate leases); New construction units built after June 1980 that are partially covered; Single‑family homes with tenancies beginning on or after Jan 1 1996 that are partially covered; Most condominiums that are partially covered; Units with certain government subsidies that are partially covered
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplex (owner‑occupied duplex as of Dec 31 1979); Unit where owner shares a kitchen or bath with tenant if owner lived on the property at tenancy start; Tenancies started after Nov 7 2018 on properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner‑occupied; University rental units such as dormitories; Nonprofit cooperative
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

rules.title: Fair Chance Screening Restrictions
rules.requirement: Housing providers receiving DND funding or income‑restricted units must not consider arrests without conviction, convictions subject to judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions older than five years when determining eligibility or eviction.
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development funding and/or land, or that have income‑restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency Inclusionary Development Policy
rules.exemptions: Does not apply when there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to safety, and does not apply to current criminal behavior.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, Department of Neighborhood Development
rules.quoted_span: The Developer/Agent (Agent) agrees to not consider any of the following categories when determining housing eligibility and or considering eviction:

rules.title: Just cause eviction requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords may evict tenants only for reasons that qualify as "just cause" under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause"

rules.title: Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources required when ending tenancy
rules.requirement: Landlords must give tenants a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time they deliver a notice to quit or a non‑renewal of lease.
rules.coverage_conditions: ALL LANDLORDS planning to end a tenancy agreement
rules.quoted_span: ALL LANDLORDS planning to end a tenancy agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources

rules.title: Prohibition on Sale and Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms for Rent Setting
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Excludes products that generate aggregated anonymous rental data, tools for establishing rent or income limits under affordable‑housing guidelines, and products used for market research, appraisal, or software development testing/training that do not use competitor data in the operational recommendation.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Prohibition on Coordinated Pricing Algorithms for Rent Setting
rules.requirement: Landlords may not sell, license, or otherwise provide coordinated pricing algorithms that set or recommend rents, nor may they use such algorithms when setting rents for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to coordinated pricing algorithms used for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Maximum application screening fee amount
rules.requirement: The fee may not exceed the applicant’s actual out‑of‑pocket costs and may not be greater than $30 per applicant.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.

rules.title: Required application screening process when charging a fee
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only if they either (A) follow a process that considers applications in the order received, provides the screening criteria in writing, approves the first applicant who meets the criteria, and charges the fee only when the application is actually considered (with a refund within seven days if not considered), or (B) return the entire fee to any applicant not selected for tenancy within seven days of selection or thirty days of submission, whichever occurs first.
rules.quoted_span: An application screening process that complies with all of the following: (i) Completed applications are considered, as provided for in the landlord’s established screening criteria, in the order in which the completed applications were received.

rules.title: Rent increase limit for residential properties
rules.requirement: An owner may raise the gross rent no more than 5% plus the cost‑of‑living increase, or 10%, whichever is lower, within any 12‑month period, and no more than two increments per 12‑month period for the same tenant.
rules.key_value: increase ≤ 5% + CPI or 10%, whichever is lower; max 2 increments per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to owners of residential real property for any dwelling or unit; limits apply over any 12‑month period and to subsequent rent increases after the initial rate is set
rules.exemptions: (1) affordable housing restricted by deed or subsidy; (2) dormitories owned by higher‑education institutions or K‑12 schools; (3) housing already subject to stricter rent‑control ordinances; (4) housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the prior 15 years (except mobilehomes); (5) residential property owned by a REIT, corporation, LLC with corporate member, or mobilehome‑park manager, provided tenants receive written notice of exemption
rules.quoted_span: shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower

rules.title: Tenant selection criteria and exemption for owner-occupied 2-family dwellings
rules.requirement: Landlords may use any reasonable standard applied uniformly to all applicants, and may consider ability to pay rent and ability to care for the apartment; the rule does not apply to 2‑family dwellings where the owner lives on the premises.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to landlords, sellers and rental agents in Cambridge
rules.exemptions: 2‑family dwellings when the owner lives there
rules.quoted_span: Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.

rules.title: Prohibition on retaliatory eviction
rules.requirement: Owners may not evict, harass, or otherwise discriminate against a tenant when the eviction is motivated by retaliation for the tenant exercising protected rights under this section.
rules.coverage_conditions: owner of any housing accommodation
rules.quoted_span: For any owner of housing accommodations to harass, evict, or otherwise discriminate against any person in the sale or rental of housing accommodations when the owner’s dominant purpose is retaliation

rules.title: Prohibit income standards that ignore household aggregate income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use a financial or income standard that fails to consider the combined income of all persons living together, as is done for married couples.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to any person using a financial or income standard in the rental of housing
rules.quoted_span: To use a financial or income standard in the rental of housing that fails to account for the aggregate income of persons residing together or proposing to reside together on the same basis as the aggregate income of married persons residing together or proposing to reside together.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords may terminate a tenancy only for the specific at‑fault or not‑at‑fault reasons listed in the ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential properties in Los Angeles not covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance; buildings newer than October 1, 1978; properties with a single‑family dwelling; tenant must have lived in unit ≥6 months or lease expired.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner’s roommate, certain cooperatives, some non‑profit homeless or substance‑abuse treatment facilities, and some HACLA or government‑owned properties.
rules.citation: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO) – Los Angeles Housing Department
rules.quoted_span: The JCO covers most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles that are not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

rules.title: Maximum Rent Increase Under AB 1482
rules.requirement: Rent increases are limited to a maximum of 8.9% for the period August 1 2024 through July 31 2025.
rules.coverage_conditions: Buildings older than 15 years
rules.quoted_span: Effective August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025, the maximum allowable increase is 8.9%.

rules.title: AB 1482 Rent Increase Limits for Buildings Over 15 Years
rules.requirement: For residential units in buildings older than 15 years, the annual rent increase may not exceed 8.9% for the period August 1 2024 through July 31 2025, and rent hikes are generally limited to the lesser of 5% plus the regional cost‑of‑living increase or 10%.
rules.key_value: max increase = 8.9% (2024‑08‑01 to 2025‑07‑31); otherwise ≤ 5% + CPI or 10%, whichever lower
rules.coverage_conditions: Buildings older than 15 years
rules.exemptions: Units constructed within the last 15 years; units restricted by deed or other affordability restrictions; certain dormitories; a two‑unit property where the second unit is occupied by the owner; single‑family homes and condominiums when (A) the property is not owned by a real estate trust, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, and (B) the landlord notifies the tenant in writing that the tenancy is not subject to just‑cause and rent‑increase limits; units already subject to the City’s RSO
rules.quoted_span: Effective August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025, the maximum allowable increase is 8.9%

rules.title: Just cause requirement for tenancy termination after 12 months occupancy
rules.requirement: An owner may not terminate a residential tenancy without stating a just cause in written notice once a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the unit for 12 months.
rules.coverage_conditions: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months; applies also when additional adult tenants are added before 24 months if either all tenants have 12 months occupancy or one or more have 24 months occupancy
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause

rules.title: Statement of cause required for termination after 12 or 24 months occupancy
rules.requirement: Landlord must provide a statement of cause in any notice to terminate a tenancy after all tenants have continuously occupied the property for 12 months or more, or after at least one tenant has continuously occupied for 24 months or more.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancy where all tenants have continuously occupied the property for 12 months or more, or at least one tenant has continuously occupied for 24 months or more.
rules.exemptions: Residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or adopted/amended after September 1, 2019 that is more protective than this section.
rules.quoted_span: after all of the tenants have continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months or more or at least one of the tenants has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 24 months or more, a landlord must provide a statement of cause

rules.title: Fourteen‑day notice to quit for nonpayment of rent
rules.requirement: Landlord must give a written 14‑day notice to quit when the tenant neglects or refuses to pay rent due under a written lease.
rules.coverage_conditions: neglect or refusal to pay rent due under a written lease
rules.exemptions: If nonpayment is caused by a failure or delay of the federal government, the commonwealth or any municipality in mailing or delivery of payment, the court shall continue the hearing at least seven days and, if rent with interest and costs is tendered within that time, treat the tenancy as not terminated
rules.quoted_span: fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease

rules.title: Security deposit limit of one month’s rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit greater than one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid before the tenant moves in.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to security for a rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant.
rules.exemptions: None expressly stated
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy

rules.title: Prohibition of nonrefundable security deposit clauses
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not include a provision that characterizes any security deposit as “nonrefundable.”
rules.quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

rules.title: Notice period for termination of estate at will for nonpayment of rent
rules.requirement: Landlords must give a written 14‑day notice to quit for nonpayment of rent, and tenants who have not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can avoid termination by paying the full rent due within 10 days.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to estates at will; if rent is payable at periods of less than three months, the notice period equals the payment interval or thirty days, whichever is longer.
rules.quoted_span: fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy;

rules.title: Maximum residential rental application fee
rules.requirement: Landlords or their agents may not charge an application or similar fee that exceeds $50 for a residential rental dwelling.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to all residential rental property applications for dwelling purposes
rules.exemptions: (1) a dwelling unit located in a one‑family or two‑family dwelling that is offered for rent; (2) a licensee of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission, unless the licensee is the landlord of the residential rental property
rules.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.

rules.title: No‑Fault Evictions Require Relocation Assistance and LAHD Declaration
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay relocation assistance and file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with the Los Angeles Housing Department before serving a notice to terminate tenancy for any not‑at‑fault eviction covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or Just Cause Ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span: All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before evicting tenants

rules.title: Escrow Requirement for Relocation Assistance Including Security Deposit
rules.requirement: Landlords must place relocation assistance monies in an escrow account within 15 days of the written eviction notice, and the escrow must be used to pay tenants for actual relocation expenses, including the security deposit.
rules.quoted_span: The escrow account must provide for payments to the tenant(s) for actual relocation expenses incurred by the tenant before vacating the unit for the following relocation expenses: first and last month’s rent; security deposit; utility connection charges; moving expenses.

rules.title: Landlord must file Declaration of Intent to Evict for JCO units when terminating for demolition
rules.requirement: When a landlord terminates a tenancy to demolish a protected unit, they must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with the LAHD for units covered by the Just Cause Ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: units regulated by the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span: File with LAHD a Declaration of Intent to Evict for units regulated by the JCO per the Los Angeles Municipal Code (LAMC) Section 165.03.I(1)

rules.title: Prohibit pre‑conditional‑offer criminal record inquiries
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not require applicants to answer criminal‑record questions or make any oral or written criminal‑record inquiry before issuing a conditional offer.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to all rental dwelling units except owner‑occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
rules.exemptions: may consider convictions for methamphetamine manufacture in federally assisted housing and lifetime sex‑offender registration requirements
rules.quoted_span: shall not require an applicant to complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer

rules.title: Disclosure of criminal‑history screening criteria before application fee
rules.requirement: Before accepting any application fee, a housing provider must give the applicant a written statement of whether criminal history will be considered and that the applicant may dispute inaccuracies or present mitigating evidence.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to all rental dwelling units except owner‑occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
rules.quoted_span: Prior to accepting any application fee, a housing provider shall disclose in writing to the applicant: (1)   Whether the eligibility criteria of the housing provider include the review and consideration of criminal history; and (2)   A statement that the applicant, pursuant to subsection a. of this section, may provide evidence demonstrating inaccuracies within the applicant's criminal record

rules.title: Restrictions on Use of Criminal Records in Applicant Screening
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not evaluate applicants based on arrests, expunged or sealed records, juvenile adjudications, or other non‑conviction information, and may only consider certain convictions after a conditional offer as specified.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all housing providers subject to C.46:8-56 of the New Jersey Fair Housing Act.
rules.exemptions: After a conditional offer, a provider may consider convictions for murder, certain sexual offenses, human trafficking, offenses resulting in lifetime sex‑offender registration, first‑degree indictable offenses within six years, second/third‑degree indictable offenses within four years, or fourth‑degree indictable offenses within one year.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not, either before or after the issuance of a conditional offer, evaluate an applicant based on any of the following types of criminal records:

rules.title: Prohibition on discriminatory advertising based on criminal records
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not publish advertisements that state they will not consider applicants with arrest or conviction records, except for drug‑related methamphetamine manufacturing on federally assisted housing and applicants subject to a lifetime sex‑offender registration.
rules.exemptions: drug‑related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing; lifetime registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not knowingly or purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses

rules.title: Prohibit drug or alcohol testing of applicants
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not require an applicant to undergo a drug or alcohol test or obtain consent to get information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.

rules.title: Return of applicant’s rental application fee
rules.requirement: The director may require that the applicant’s rental application fee be returned.
rules.quoted_span: (3)   Unless housing is provided to the applicant pursuant to paragraph (2) of this subsection, the director may require that the applicant’s rental application fee be returned;

rules.title: Notice period for eviction after successful appeal
rules.requirement: If a housing provider’s appeal is successful and the court overturns the director’s order, the provider must give the applicant at least 45 days’ notice before eviction.
rules.coverage_conditions: if an appeal by a housing provider is successful and the court overturns a final decision of the director
rules.quoted_span: so long as the housing provider provides the applicant with at least 45 days’ notice prior to the eviction;

rules.title: Rent parity for handicap-accessible housing
rules.requirement: Owners may not charge higher rent for handicap-accessible units than for comparable non‑accessible units.
rules.coverage_conditions: handicap-accessible housing
rules.quoted_span: there shall not be established or imposed a rent or other charge for such handicap-accessible housing which is higher than the rent or other charge for comparable nonaccessible housing

rules.title: Limits on security deposits and fees in lieu of deposits
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord may only charge rent for the first month, rent for the last month at the same rate, and a security deposit equal to one month’s rent, or an optional fee in lieu of the deposit that cannot exceed one month’s rent.
rules.key_value: security deposit = 1 month's rent; fee in lieu ≤ 1 month's rent
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to all residential leases at or prior to commencement of tenancy
rules.quoted_span: no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:

rules.title: Security deposit amount limit
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand a security deposit greater than the amount allowed by this section.
rules.quoted_span: No lessor or successor in interest shall at any time subsequent to the commencement of a tenancy demand rent in advance in excess of the current month's rent or a security deposit in excess of the amount allowed by this section.

rules.title: Ban on Automated Rent-Setting Software
rules.requirement: The ordinance would prohibit the sale, licensing, and use of any automated rent‑setting software that advises or recommends rental rates or occupancy levels.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies citywide to all rental properties in San Diego
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code (proposed) Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 11, §§ 98.1101‑98.1104
rules.quoted_span: banning the sale, license, and use of automated rent-setting software that advises or recommends rental rates or occupancy levels

rules.title: Ban on algorithmic rent price‑setting devices
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale, licensing, and use of algorithmic devices that set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental properties.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to residential rental properties
rules.exemptions: does not ban software that publishes aggregated public rental data or software used for affordable housing program guidelines
rules.citation: San Diego City Council, Proposed Anti‑Competitive Automated Rent Price‑Fixing Prohibition Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The proposed ordinance bans the sale, licensing, and use of an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental properties.

rules.title: Prohibition of sale, licensing, and use of algorithmic devices for rent setting
rules.requirement: The ordinance prohibits the sale, licensing, and use of algorithmic devices that use nonpublic competitor data to advise landlords on rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property in San Diego.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any algorithmic device that uses or incorporates nonpublic competitor data concerning rental rates, occupancy levels, or other leasing information for residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Software or product used to publish reports from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old, or from publicly available information, that does not recommend future rental rates or occupancy levels.
rules.quoted_span: prohibiting the sale, licensing, and use of algorithmic devices that use or incorporate nonpublic competitor data to advise a landlord on, or recommend to a landlord, rental rates or occupancy levels

rules.title: Prohibition on Landlord Use of Algorithmic Devices for Rental Pricing
rules.requirement: A landlord may not use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to any landlord in San Diego using an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.

rules.title: Prohibition on Sale, Licensing, and Use of Algorithmic Devices for Rental Pricing
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord, and unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to any person selling or licensing an algorithmic device to a landlord, and to landlords using such devices for residential rental property in the City of San Diego
rules.exemptions: algorithmic device does not include (a) software used to publish reports from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or public information, and (b) software used to establish rates or income limits in accordance with affordable housing program guidelines
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord.

rules.title: Prohibition of algorithmic devices for rent setting
rules.requirement: Landlords may not sell or use algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to residential units in San Francisco
rules.citation: Section 37.10C of the San Francisco Rent Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: the law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco

rules.title: Just Cause Requirement for Eviction
rules.requirement: Landlords may evict a tenant only if they have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive, and the reason must be one of the 17 enumerated causes; mere lease expiration or change in ownership does not qualify.
rules.coverage_conditions: rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.

rules.title: Annual allowable rent increase for rent‑controlled units (2026‑2027)
rules.requirement: Rent‑controlled units may increase rent by up to 1.6% of the base rent for the period March 1 2026 through February 28 2027.
rules.coverage_conditions: rent‑controlled units
rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Board, Annual Rent Increase Announcement, Jan 14 2026
rules.quoted_span: For rent‑controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.

rules.title: Just cause requirement for tenancy termination
rules.requirement: Landlords must have a legally recognized just cause to terminate a tenancy, as required by this Division and consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2.
rules.quoted_span: requiring just cause for termination of a tenancy consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2

rules.title: Exemptions from Just Cause Eviction Requirements
rules.requirement: The division does not apply to the listed types of residential rental properties or circumstances.
rules.exemptions: (a) transient and tourist hotel occupancy; (b) short‑term residential occupancy; (c) housing restricted by deed or regulatory agreement for very low, low, or moderate income; (d) housing subsidized for affordable housing (excluding Section 8); (e) mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law; (f) accommodations in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended‑care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities, or nonprofit transitional housing; (g) dormitories owned and operated by higher‑education institutions; (h) rental property where tenant shares bathroom or kitchen with landlord who lives on‑site; (i) single‑family residence occupied by landlord as principal residence (renting no more than two bedrooms, ADUs, or junior ADUs, or a mobilehome); (j) property with two separate units in one structure where landlord occupies one unit; (k) housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); (l) rental property alienable from other dwelling units where landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome‑park management.
rules.quoted_span: This Division shall not apply to the following types of residential rental properties or residential circumstances:

rules.title: Just cause required for termination
rules.requirement: Landlords may only terminate a tenancy for specified just‑cause reasons, which include both at‑fault and no‑fault grounds listed in the code.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.

rules.title: Exemption from just cause requirements
rules.requirement: Properties that meet section 98.0703(l) and whose landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobile‑home‑park management are exempt from the just‑cause eviction rules.
rules.coverage_conditions: property meets the requirements of San Diego Municipal Code section 98.0703(l) and the landlord is not any of the listed entities
rules.quoted_span: This property is not subject to the just cause requirements of Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7 of the San Diego Municipal Code. This property meets the requirements of San Diego Municipal Code section 98.0703(l) and the landlord is not any of the following: (1) a real estate investment trust

rules.title: Owner personal occupancy termination requirement
rules.requirement: For leases entered on or after June 24, 2023, termination under section 98.0704(b)(1) is allowed only if the tenant agrees in writing or the lease expressly permits the owner to terminate to occupy the unit for the owner or immediate family.
rules.coverage_conditions: leases entered into on or after June 24, 2023
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7, Section 98.0704
rules.quoted_span: For leases entered into on or after June 24, 2023, section 98.0704(b)(1) shall apply only if the tenant agrees to the termination in writing or if the lease expressly allows the owner to terminate the lease if the owner unilaterally decides to occupy the residential rental property for the owner or their spouse, domestic partner, child (by blood or adoption), grandchild (by blood or adoption), parent, or grandparent.

rules.title: Just cause eviction notice requirements for demolition or substantial remodel
rules.requirement: A written notice terminating tenancy for just cause must include a statement of intent to demolish or substantially remodel, an offer to re‑rent at the same terms if work is not commenced or completed, a description of the work and its expected duration, a copy of required permits or contractor agreement, a statement why the tenant must vacate for at least 30 continuous days, and a notification required by section 98.0706(b)(1)(C).
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when landlord intends to demolish or substantially remodel the residential rental property, requiring the tenant to vacate for at least 30 continuous days.
rules.quoted_span: A written notice terminating a tenancy for just cause under section 98.0704(b)(4) shall include all the following, certified under penalty of perjury:

rules.title: At-Fault Just Cause Termination Notice Requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords must give the tenant a written notice describing the curable lease violation and an opportunity to cure, then provide a three‑day notice to quit if not cured; they must also notify the Commission within three business days after the tenant notice.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential rental property subject to this Division
rules.quoted_span: If a landlord issues a termination notice for at-fault just cause, the landlord shall do the following:

rules.title: No-Fault Just Cause Termination Notice Requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords must give tenants written notice at least 30 or 60 days before termination, in at least 12‑point font, describing the basis for termination and informing tenants of relocation assistance and renewal offer rights.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential rental property subject to this Division
rules.quoted_span: If a landlord issues a termination notice for no-fault just cause, the landlord shall do the following:

rules.title: Landlord must notify Commission of no‑fault just cause termination
rules.requirement: The landlord shall provide written notice to the Commission of the no‑fault just cause termination no later than three business days after giving the required notice to the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to no‑fault just cause terminations under section 98.0704(b).
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall provide written notice to the Commission of the no-fault just cause termination of tenancy under section 98.0704(b) no later than three business days after the date the landlord provided the required notice to tenant.

rules.title: Relocation assistance payment amount
rules.requirement: The landlord shall provide a direct payment equal to two months of rent, or three months if the tenant is senior or disabled.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to no‑fault just cause terminations under section 98.0704(b).
rules.quoted_span: Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.

rules.title: Displaced tenant must be offered the unit first
rules.requirement: If the property is offered for rent within five years of a no‑fault eviction, the landlord must first offer the unit in writing to the displaced tenant who notifies within 30 days and provides a mailing or email address.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when a residential rental property is offered for rent within five years of an eviction under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4).
rules.quoted_span: If a residential rental property is offered for rent or lease for residential purposes within five years of the date the tenant was evicted under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4), landlord shall first offer to lease the residential rental property in writing to the tenant displaced from that unit by the no-fault just cause termination if the tenant:

rules.title: Landlord must communicate minimum screening criteria
rules.requirement: The landlord shall communicate the minimum screening criteria in the written offer for the new tenancy.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when offering a unit to a displaced tenant under the no‑fault just cause provision.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall have the right to screen the tenant using industry accepted methods and shall communicate the minimum screening criteria in the written offer for the new tenancy.

rules.title: Return of security deposit required in addition to relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Relocation assistance does not relieve the landlord’s obligation to return any deposit or security amounts owed to the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to relocations required under this Division (no‑fault just cause terminations).
rules.quoted_span: The relocation assistance required by this Division shall not relieve the landlord’s obligation to, and shall be in addition to, the return of any deposit or security amounts owed to the tenant.

rules.title: Wrongful eviction damages for illegal possession recovery
rules.requirement: Landlords who attempt to recover possession of a residential rental property in violation of this Division are liable for damages of at least three times the actual economic damages.
rules.key_value: damages not less than three times the actual economic damages
rules.coverage_conditions: attempt to recover possession of a residential rental property in violation of this Division
rules.quoted_span: Any attempt by a landlord to recover possession of a residential rental property in violation of this Division shall render the landlord liable to the tenant in a civil action for wrongful eviction for damages of not less than three times the actual economic damages.

rules.title: Just cause required for lease non‑renewal
rules.requirement: A landlord may not refuse to renew a lease unless the landlord has good cause not to renew.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental properties except owner‑occupied two‑ or three‑family dwellings, motels, hotels, transient or seasonal units
rules.exemptions: Owner‑occupied two‑ or three‑family dwellings, motels, hotels, transient or seasonal units are exempt
rules.quoted_span: No landlord of residential rental properties except t hose in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.

rules.title: Security deposit return timeline and notice requirements after lease termination due to domestic violence
rules.requirement: Landlord must make the security deposit plus any interest available within 15 business days after the lease is terminated, must notify the tenant in writing within three business days of where and when to pick it up, and must keep the deposit available for 30 days with an itemized statement of interest and deductions.
rules.coverage_conditions: lease terminated pursuant to the Safe Housing Act (N.J.S.A. 46:8-9.6)
rules.quoted_span: Within 15 business days after the lease  is terminated, the landlord shall make available the return of the tenant’s security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant’s agent.

rules.title: Return of security deposit for service‑member lease terminations
rules.requirement: Landlords must return the security deposit to the tenant in accordance with N.J.S.A. 46:8-26 when the lease is terminated under the Service Members Civil Relief Act.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to service members terminating a lease under the Service Members Civil Relief Act
rules.quoted_span: The landlord is required to return the security deposit in accordance with the applicable Security Deposit Law (N.J.S.A. 46:8-26).

rules.title: Maximum security deposit amount
rules.requirement: A landlord may collect a security deposit no greater than one and one‑half times one month’s rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, except owner‑occupied two‑ or three‑family dwellings unless the tenant requests coverage in writing.
rules.exemptions: Owner‑occupied two‑ or three‑family dwellings (unless tenant requests the law apply).
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

rules.title: Interest payment and notice requirements for security deposits
rules.requirement: Interest earned on a security deposit belongs to the tenant and must be paid in cash or credited to rent, with annual notice of account details provided within 30 days of receipt and each interest payment.
rules.key_value: interest payable to tenant; 30‑day notice of account
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all security deposits covered by the law, excluding seasonal rentals.
rules.exemptions: Seasonal use or rental deposits are excluded.
rules.quoted_span: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and shall be paid to the tenant in cash or credited toward rent ... Within 30 days of receipt of the security deposit and at the time of each annual interest payment, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the name and address of the banking institution...

rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days after tenancy termination
rules.requirement: Landlord must return the security deposit plus earned interest, less any lawful deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends and must provide an itemized list of deductions.
rules.coverage_conditions: after termination of tenancy
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant

rules.title: Return period delayed when tenant breaks lease without legal cause
rules.requirement: When a tenant breaks the lease without legal cause, the 30‑day return period for the security deposit does not begin until the unit is re‑rented or the lease expires, whichever occurs first.
rules.coverage_conditions: tenant breaks lease without legal cause
rules.citation: J.C. Mitchell v. First Real Estate, 287 N.J. Super 546 (1996)
rules.quoted_span: the 30 days that the landlord shall return the tenant’s security deposit does not start until the landlord re‑rents the rental unit, or until the lease expires

rules.title: New owner’s responsibility for security deposit upon property transfer
rules.requirement: When a property is sold or transferred, the new owner must obtain the existing security deposit plus accrued interest and is responsible for its investment, notice requirements, interest payments, and eventual return.
rules.coverage_conditions: property is sold or transferred
rules.quoted_span: If the property is sold or transferred it is the duty of the new owner to obtain the security deposit, plus accrued interest on the tenant’s deposit, that was collected by the former owner

rules.title: Security deposit dispute jurisdiction thresholds
rules.requirement: Disputes involving security deposits of $5,000 or less must be filed in the Small Claims section of the Special Civil Part of the Superior Court, Law Division in the county where the unit is located or where the landlord resides; disputes over $5,000 but not exceeding $15,000 must be filed in the Special Civil Part of the Superior Court Law Division.
rules.quoted_span: The Small Claims section of the Special Civil Part of the Superior Court, Law Division in the county where the unit is located or in the county where the landlord resides has jurisdiction in actions involving security deposits where the amount does not exceed $5,000

rules.title: Civil penalty for withholding security deposits of assisted tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord who willfully withholds a security deposit made on behalf of a tenant receiving state or federal financial assistance is liable for a civil penalty of $500 to $2,000 per offense.
rules.coverage_conditions: tenant receiving financial assistance through any State or federal program
rules.quoted_span: Any landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds a security deposit made by or on behalf of a tenant who has received financial assistance through any State or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance , may be penalized. The landlord may be liable for a civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense.

rules.title: Criminal penalty for unlawful use of security deposit monies
rules.requirement: Any person who unlawfully uses security deposit monies may be charged as a disorderly person and face a fine of at least $200, imprisonment up to 30 days, or both.
rules.quoted_span: Any person who unlawfully uses security deposit monies may be criminally charged as a disorderly person and may be subject to a fine of not less than $200 or imprisonment for not more than 30 days, or both

rules.title: Landlords may charge applicants for cost of credit report
rules.requirement: Landlords are permitted to charge tenants the cost of obtaining a credit report used in the rental application.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord is allowed to charge the tenant for the cost of the report.

rules.title: Rent increase notice and unconscionability requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord must give the tenant proper written notice of a lease termination and rent increase, cannot raise rent mid‑lease, and any increase must not be unconscionable or violate municipal rent‑control ordinances.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential leases in New Jersey, except newly constructed multiple dwellings (30‑year exemption) and HUD‑subsidized housing.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt for 30 years after construction; rents subsidized by governmental funding and HUD‑subsidized housing are also exempt.
rules.quoted_span: The increase in rent must not be unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

rules.title: Landlord registration required to evict tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict a tenant unless the landlord has filed the required registration statement.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to landlords of one- or two-family non-owner-occupied homes and buildings with three or more units
rules.exemptions: Owner‑occupied two‑family homes are not required to be registered.
rules.quoted_span: the landlord registration law prohibits a landlord from evicting a tenant in the building if the landlord has not been properly registered (N.J.S.A. 46:8-27 to -37)

rules.title: Security deposit return upon constructive eviction
rules.requirement: If a tenant invokes constructive eviction and the landlord is found negligent in maintaining the rental unit, the tenant is entitled to the return of the security deposit and is not responsible for the rent for the balance of the lease.
rules.coverage_conditions: if a tenant invokes constructive eviction and the landlord is found negligent in maintaining the rental unit
rules.quoted_span: the tenant is entitled t o the return of the security deposit and is not responsible for the rent

rules.title: Good cause required for eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant only for a statutory “good cause” and must provide a written Notice to Quit for all good‑cause evictions except nonpayment of rent.
rules.exemptions: Nonpayment of rent does not require a Notice to Quit.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53). There are several grounds for a good cause eviction.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act – Good‑Cause Requirement for Eviction or Non‑Renewal
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a lease unless the landlord can prove good cause in court.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties including single‑family homes, mobile homes, apartment buildings, complexes, and rooming or boarding homes (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53 to -84).
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to two‑ or three‑unit owner‑occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; hotel, motel, or guest‑house guests who are transient or seasonal; and units held in trust for an immediate family member who is developmentally disabled and permanently occupies the unit.
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.

rules.title: Failure to Pay Rent – Notice Requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords may file an eviction suit for nonpayment without prior notice, except for tenants in federally subsidized housing who must receive a 14‑day notice.
rules.coverage_conditions: tenant resides in federally subsidized housing
rules.quoted_span: The landlord is not required to give the tenant notice before filing an eviction suit, except if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing. I f the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing a 14-day notice must be given before filing a suite for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(a)).

rules.title: Disorderly Conduct – Notice to Quit
rules.requirement: Landlords must serve a Notice to Quit at least three days before filing an eviction suit for disorderly conduct.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(b)).

rules.title: Substantial Violation of Rules – Notice to Quit
rules.requirement: Landlords must serve a Notice to Quit at least one month before filing an eviction suit for substantial lease rule violations, and the notice must be given on or before the start of a new month.
rules.key_value: 1‑month notice; notice on/before start of month
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction. In addition, any notices must be given on or before the start of a new month (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(d)).

rules.title: Rent increase must not be unconscionable
rules.requirement: A rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control.
rules.quoted_span: the rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances

rules.title: Eviction for illegal drug activity in public housing
rules.requirement: In public housing, a landlord may file a suit for eviction if the tenant substantially violated lease covenants related to illegal drug activity, without needing to give a Notice to Cease.
rules.coverage_conditions: public housing
rules.quoted_span: the landlord may file a suit for eviction. The covenant or agreement must conform to federal guidelines and must have been in effect at the beginning of the lease term. The landlord does not have to give Notice to Cease the illegal activity before filing a Notice to Quit

rules.title: Eviction for failure to pay rent after rent increase notice
rules.requirement: If a tenant fails to pay rent after being given notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit, the landlord may file a suit for eviction.
rules.quoted_span: If a tenant fails to pay rent after being given notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit, the landlord may file a suit for eviction

rules.title: Eviction for health and safety violations requiring removal
rules.requirement: A tenant may be evicted when the landlord is cited for substantial health and safety violations that require boarding up, demolition, or cannot be abated while the tenant resides, with a Notice to Quit served at least three months before filing suit.
rules.coverage_conditions: landlord cited for health and safety violations; property removal or inability to abate
rules.quoted_span: A tenant may be evicted if the following conditions apply: 1) The landlord has been cited by an inspector and needs to board up or demolish the property because of substantial health and safety violations ... A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit for eviction

rules.title: Eviction for landlord permanently retiring property
rules.requirement: If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use, a Notice to Quit must be served at least 18 months prior, and no legal action may be taken until the lease expires.
rules.quoted_span: If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months prior to filing the suit for eviction

rules.title: One‑month notice before eviction for lease‑change refusal
rules.requirement: When a tenant refuses reasonable lease changes after written notice, the landlord must serve a Notice to Quit at least one month before filing an eviction suit.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month before filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(i)).

rules.title: One‑month notice before eviction for habitual non‑payment
rules.requirement: If a tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, the landlord must serve a Notice to Quit at least one month before filing an eviction suit.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(j)).

rules.title: Three‑year notice before eviction for conversion to condo/co‑op
rules.requirement: When a landlord converts a rental property to a condominium, cooperative, or fee‑simple ownership, a Notice to Quit must be served at least three years before filing an eviction suit.
rules.exemptions: No action for possession shall be brought against a senior citizen tenant or disabled tenant with protected tenancy status pursuant to the “Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act of 1992,” as long as the agency has not terminated the protected tenancy status or the protected tenancy period has not expired.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three years before filing a suit for eviction.

rules.title: Two‑month notice before eviction after conversion to condo/co‑op
rules.requirement: For tenants whose tenancy began after a property was recorded as a condominium, cooperative, or fee‑simple ownership, the landlord must serve a Notice to Quit at least two months before filing an eviction suit.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least two months prior to filing suit for eviction.

rules.title: Eviction for Property Conversion
rules.requirement: Landlord must give a Notice to Quit at least two months before filing an eviction suit and cannot take legal action until the lease ends.
rules.coverage_conditions: tenant was given a statement that the property is being converted
rules.quoted_span: Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least two months prior to filing suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires.

rules.title: Eviction for Termination of Employment‑Based Tenancy
rules.requirement: If a tenant’s tenancy is based on employment (e.g., superintendent, janitor) and that employment ends, the landlord may evict after giving a three‑day Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_conditions: tenant resides on the condition of employment by the landlord as a superintendent, janitor, or other job
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).

rules.title: Eviction for Conviction of Drug Offense on the Property
rules.requirement: Landlord may evict a tenant convicted of a drug offense on the property unless the tenant has completed or is participating in a rehabilitation program; a three‑day Notice to Quit is required.
rules.coverage_conditions: tenant convicted of or pleaded guilty to drug offenses that took place on the property and has not completed or is not in a rehab program
rules.exemptions: does not apply to a tenant allowing a juvenile to reside at the property where the juvenile has been found delinquent due to use or possession of drugs
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(n)).

rules.title: Eviction for Conviction of Assault or Threat Against Landlord
rules.requirement: Landlord may evict a tenant convicted of assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, family, or employees, after giving a three‑day Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_conditions: tenant convicted of or pleaded guilty to assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, a family member, or an employee
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three day s prior to filing a suit for (N.J.S.A. 2A-18-61.1(o)).

rules.title: Eviction for drug‑related convictions
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant who has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to a drug‑related offense, provided a three‑day Notice to Quit is served before filing the eviction suit.
rules.coverage_conditions: tenant convicted of a drug offense or permits a convicted person to reside; also applies to juveniles found delinquent due to drug use
rules.exemptions: does not apply to a tenant allowing a juvenile to reside where the juvenile’s delinquency is due to the use or possession of drugs
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction. This does not apply to a tenant allowing a juvenile to reside at the property where the juvenile has been found to be delinquent due to the use or possession of drugs.

rules.title: Eviction for theft convictions
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant who has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to theft of property, with a three‑day Notice to Quit required before filing suit.
rules.coverage_conditions: tenant convicted of theft of property or permits a convicted person to reside; also applies to juveniles found delinquent for theft
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to, or if a juvenile has been found to be delinquent by the Court due to an offense involving theft of property... A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(q)).

rules.title: Eviction for human‑trafficking violations
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant who has committed a human‑trafficking violation or harbors a trafficker, with a three‑day Notice to Quit and a two‑year limitation on bringing the action.
rules.coverage_conditions: tenant found to have committed human‑trafficking violation or knowingly harbors a trafficker
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant in a civil action is found to have committed a violation of the human trafficking provisions... No action for removal pursuant to this subsection may be brought more than two years after the alleged violation has terminated (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(r)).

rules.title: Evictions for owner‑occupied two‑ and three‑family dwellings
rules.requirement: Landlords of owner‑occupied two‑ or three‑family dwellings may evict only for specific lease violations and must give a three‑month notice for at‑will or year‑to‑year tenancies, a one‑month notice for month‑to‑month tenancies, and a three‑day notice for disorderly or destructive conduct.
rules.key_value: three‑month notice for at‑will/year‑to‑year; one‑month notice for month‑to‑month; three‑day notice for disorderly/destructive violations
rules.coverage_conditions: tenants of landlord‑occupied two‑ and three‑family dwellings
rules.quoted_span: A three (3) month notice to quit must be given if an at will tenancy or year‑to‑year tenancy exists. A one (1) month notice to quit is required for a month‑to‑month tenancy... A three‑day written Notice to Quit is required for any of the causes described as disorderly, destructive or violative of written rules or lease provisions (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2(a)).

rules.title: Rooming and boarding house eviction requirements
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming or boarding houses must follow the good‑cause and notice requirements of the Eviction Law and must give at least three working days’ notice to the County Welfare Board before commencing an eviction action.
rules.key_value: three working days notice to County Welfare Board
rules.coverage_conditions: owners of rooming or boarding houses (buildings with at least two unrelated living units without private kitchens/bathrooms)
rules.quoted_span: require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents... There is a further requirement that the owner give at least three (3) working days’ notice to the County Welfare Board before starting the eviction action for any resident (N.J.A.C. 5:26-3.4(c)).

rules.title: 90‑day notice required before eviction for foreclosure buyer occupancy
rules.requirement: Landlords must give a 90‑day notice to quit when a foreclosed property is purchased by a buyer who will personally occupy it as a primary residence.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies when the foreclosed property is purchased by a buyer who intends to occupy it as a primary residence; month‑to‑month tenants and two‑ and three‑family owner‑occupied units are not exempt
rules.quoted_span: the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90‑day notice to quit when the foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her primary residence

rules.title: Prohibition on excessive rent increase as pressure tactic
rules.requirement: Landlords may not increase rent beyond any rent control or rent‑leveling ordinance, and if the property is not subject to rent control, they may not impose an unreasonable or unconscionable rent increase when making a monetary offer to vacate.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies when a landlord makes a bona fide monetary offer to vacate the tenant's unit
rules.quoted_span: An increase in rent in excess of any rent control or rent leveling ordinance, or if the property is not subject to rent control, an unreasonable or unconscionable rent increase.

rules.title: CA AB 325 / SB 763 — Prohibition on Common Pricing Algorithms (Cartwright Act)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for any person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in California. It is also unlawful to coerce another person to set or adopt a price recommended by such an algorithm. Applies statewide, including to apartment rental pricing.
rules.key_value: Criminal fines up to $6M (businesses) / $1M (individuals); civil fines up to $1M.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person (including landlords and rent-setting software providers) who uses or distributes a 'common pricing algorithm' — defined as any methodology, including software or technology, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price. Single-firm algorithms using only a business's own data are NOT covered.
rules.exemptions: Single-firm algorithms using only the business's own proprietary data are exempt. The law does not affect independent pricing decisions uncoordinated through shared algorithms.
rules.interaction: Operates alongside local city-level algorithmic pricing bans in San Francisco, San Diego, Berkeley, and Santa Ana. Local bans may impose stricter standards.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

rules.title: NJ FAIR Act — Statewide Prohibition on Algorithmic Rent-Setting (P.L.2026, c.43)
rules.requirement: The Fostering Affordability and Integrity in Rental (FAIR) Act prohibits landlords and property managers from using algorithmic rent-setting software that incorporates nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents in New Jersey. Enacted July 20, 2026; effective July 1, 2027.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental properties in New Jersey where landlords or their agents use software or algorithmic tools that incorporate nonpublic competitor rental pricing data to set, recommend, or stabilize rents.
rules.exemptions: Algorithms using only a landlord's own historical data without incorporating nonpublic competitor data are not covered.
rules.interaction: Possible preemption conflict with local bans in Hoboken (ch. 158, Art. II, eff. Jul 2025) and Jersey City (§218-12, eff. Jun 2025). Both local bans are currently in force. It is legally contested whether the FAIR Act, when it takes effect, will preempt the stricter local bans or coexist with them.
rules.citation: N.J. P.L.2026, c.43 (FAIR Act), signed July 20, 2026, effective July 1, 2027.
rules.quoted_span: New Jersey Enacts FAIR Act to Prohibit Algorithmic Rent-Setting Practices. The law prohibits landlords from using algorithmic rent-setting software that incorporates nonpublic competitor data.
rules.conflict_note: Preemption Conflict: The NJ FAIR Act (eff. 2027-07-01) may preempt or conflict with local algorithmic pricing bans in Hoboken and Jersey City, which are currently in force. Legal status of local bans after FAIR Act takes effect is contested.
